transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came because everybody keeps acting like I’m the problem, like I’m making things up, but I’m not. My family and my friends keep telling me the bank papers prove nothing was taken, like if they wave some papers at me that’s supposed to settle it. But I know what’s been going on. It’s been over a year now, and I’ve been watching it and putting it together.

They’re hiding my money. They use all these excuses — bills coming up, fundraisers, trips they’re planning — and somehow it always circles back to why money is missing or why I shouldn’t ask questions. And then when I do ask, they say, “Look at the papers,” like papers can’t be fixed or used to cover things. I keep confronting them because what else am I supposed to do? Just sit there and let them lie to my face?

I’m here because they keep saying I need to talk to someone, but honestly I need someone to understand that I just want the truth. I need them to finally admit what they did.
Have you been hearing voices when no one is there?

No… I mean, not like that. I don’t sit in a room and hear somebody talking when nobody’s there, if that’s what you mean. People keep trying to make it sound like I’m hearing things or imagining things, but that’s not what’s happening.

What I’m talking about is what people say to me and what they do, the way they act, the way they change the story. I hear them just fine when they’re actually there. But voices out of nowhere? No, I haven’t noticed anything like that.
Have there been times when your mood felt unusually high or unusually irritable for days at a time?

I don’t know… I mean, I get irritated, yes, but anybody would be irritated if people kept acting like you’re crazy when you’re just asking questions. So if you mean have I been in some kind of happy, excited mood for days, like feeling on top of the world or something, no, I don’t think so.

I’ve had days where I’m worked up because I’m thinking about everything and trying to get people to stop lying to me, but that’s not the same as being in some strange high mood. It’s more like frustration, because I keep getting pushed into defending myself. So… unusually high, no. Irritable, maybe, but I think there’s a reason for it.
Is it possible that you might be mistaken about your family stealing your money?

No, I don’t think I’m mistaken. I know people keep wanting me to say that, like if I just admit maybe I’m wrong then everybody can stop talking about it and pretend everything is fine. But it isn’t fine.

I’ve been watching this for over a year. It’s not like I woke up one morning and just decided my family was stealing from me. It’s the way they explain things, the way money is suddenly tied up in bills, or somebody has a fundraiser, or there’s some trip being talked about, and then when I ask where my money is or why something doesn’t add up, they shove bank papers at me like that proves everything. But papers don’t tell the whole story. People can hide things behind papers.

And my friends are doing it too, or at least they keep backing them up, saying, “Nothing was taken, look at the records,” like I’m stupid. I’m not stupid. I know when people are covering for each other. So no, I don’t really think I’m mistaken. I think they want me to doubt myself so I’ll stop confronting them. But I’m not going to stop until they tell the truth.
Before all of this with the money, have you generally tended to distrust other people?

I don’t know… I mean, what do you mean by “distrust”? Because I don’t think I walked around thinking everybody was out to get me or anything like that, if that’s what you’re asking. I’ve always been the kind of person who watches how people act, maybe, and I don’t just believe every word somebody says because people do lie sometimes. That’s just life.

But before all this, I don’t know that I would’ve called myself a suspicious person. I wasn’t sitting there keeping score on everybody. I had people around me, I talked to people. I guess I could be careful with people if something didn’t feel right, but I don’t think that’s the same as distrusting everybody. It’s hard to answer because now everybody acts like anything I say means I had some problem all along, and I don’t think that’s fair.
During this past year, have you had a period where you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

I don’t know if I’d call it depressed most of the day nearly every day. I mean, I’ve been upset a lot, yes. There are days where I wake up already tired of having to think about all this, and I feel worn down because it’s like nobody listens to me and everybody wants to turn it around on me. But depressed like… just sad all day for no reason, every day? I’m not sure that’s what it is.

It’s more like I get angry, or hurt, or exhausted from having to keep explaining myself. Some days I don’t feel like dealing with people because I already know what they’re going to say. But I don’t know how to separate that from what’s been going on. If people were treating me honestly, I don’t think I’d feel this way.

So… I guess I’ve had bad days, a lot of stress, but I can’t say there was one clear period where I was depressed nearly every day all day. Not like that.
Have other people told you that your speech is hard to follow or that you jump from one idea to another in a way that doesn’t make sense to them?

I don’t think so. I mean, people say I “go on” about things, sure, because they don’t want to hear the whole explanation. They want me to answer everything in two words, and some things don’t fit into two words. If I’m trying to explain what happened or why something doesn’t add up, I have to include the parts that connect, otherwise they act like I’m just making accusations out of nowhere.

But hard to follow? I don’t know. Nobody has really said it like that to me. They might get impatient or say, “You’re not making sense,” but I think that’s more because they don’t like what I’m saying, not because I’m jumping around for no reason. I know what I mean when I’m talking. Sometimes I have to back up and explain the beginning, then the middle, because people keep interrupting or pretending they don’t understand.

So… no, I haven’t noticed my speech being hard to follow like that. People just don’t listen right.
Have you felt that other people can read your thoughts?

Read my thoughts? No… I don’t think so. I mean, I don’t know how that would even work, exactly. Sometimes people act like they know what I’m going to say before I say it, or they jump in and assume what I mean, and that bothers me because it’s like they’ve already decided what I’m thinking. But that’s not the same as actually reading my thoughts, I guess.

I’ve had people look at me a certain way, like they think they’ve got me figured out, and I’ll be sitting there thinking, “You don’t know what’s in my head.” But I wouldn’t say I feel like they can literally hear my thoughts or anything like that. It’s more that people make assumptions and then treat those assumptions like facts. So… no, not really.
Aside from your family and friends hiding your money, have you believed that anyone else was trying to harm you or plot against you?

I mean… yes, but it’s mostly connected to the money. It’s not like I walk around thinking every stranger is after me or something. It’s people who are involved, or who know what’s going on and won’t admit it. My family and some friends keep acting like I’m making it up because they say the bank papers don’t show anything was taken, but those papers don’t explain everything. They keep pointing to the papers like that’s supposed to end the conversation, and it doesn’t.

For over a year I’ve known they’ve been hiding my money. They cover it up with bills, and these little stories about fundraisers, and trip plans, like money is going here or there, but it never adds up right. Then when I ask questions, they act offended or say I’m being difficult. That feels like plotting to me, because if nobody did anything wrong, why keep dodging it? Why keep making it look like the money went toward normal things?

That’s why I keep confronting them. I know everyone says I should stop bringing it up, but I can’t just let people lie to my face and then tell me I’m the problem. I’m not saying someone is going to jump out and hurt me, but I do believe they’re working together to keep the truth from me until I get tired and drop it. And I’m not going to, because I need them to finally tell the truth.
Have you noticed yourself becoming much less interested in things you used to care about?

I don’t know… I wouldn’t say I’ve become much less interested, exactly. I mean, some things feel harder to enjoy when there’s all this stress and people keep acting like I’m the one causing problems, but that’s different from not caring anymore.

Like, I still care about the things I cared about. I still notice them. I still want things to be normal. It’s just sometimes my mind is busy with everything else, so maybe I don’t sit and do things the same way I used to. But I don’t think I’ve lost interest in everything or anything like that.

So… no, not really. Not that I’ve noticed.
During this past year, have there been times when you were much more active than usual, constantly taking on tasks or pursuing plans?

Much more active than usual? I don’t think so… not in the way you’re saying, like constantly taking on tasks or making all these plans. I mean, I’ve had times where I’m busy or I’m trying to get things sorted out, but I wouldn’t say I suddenly had all this extra energy or started doing a bunch of things I normally wouldn’t do.

Sometimes if there’s something on my mind, I’ll keep going over it and I might make calls or try to organize things or write stuff down, but that feels more like I’m trying to handle what’s in front of me, not like I’m just full of energy and chasing plans. I’m not someone who’s out there starting ten projects or running around doing everything. So… no, I haven’t really noticed that.
Have you ever felt that thoughts were being put into your mind by someone or something outside you?

No… I don’t think it’s like thoughts being put in my mind. It’s not like some outside thing is placing words in my head or controlling what I think.

What I’m saying is different. I came in because my family and friends keep acting like the bank papers prove nothing happened, like that should just shut me up, but those papers don’t explain where the money really went. For over a year I’ve known they’ve been hiding it, and then they cover it with bills, fundraisers, trip plans, all these reasons that sound normal if you don’t look too closely. But I do look closely, and it doesn’t add up.

So the thoughts aren’t being put there by somebody else. I’m thinking about it because it’s happening, and because they keep denying it. That’s why I keep confronting them. I need them to stop hiding behind paperwork and excuses and just tell the truth.
Did this belief that your family was hiding your money come on suddenly?

Not suddenly, no. It wasn’t like one day I woke up and thought that out of nowhere. It’s been going on since my income dropped… about a year and two months ago, something like that.

That’s when things started not making sense to me. I kept noticing the money situation wasn’t lining up, and the more time went on, the more it felt like people were explaining it away instead of actually answering me. So it built up from there. It’s been over a year now, not some sudden thing.
Have you felt that someone or something was controlling your actions or movements?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, nobody is moving my arms or making me walk somewhere or anything like that. I’m in control of what I do.

Sometimes people pressure you, you know, or they keep saying things until you feel pushed to respond, but that’s not the same as controlling my body. If I make a call or go somewhere or say something, that’s me doing it because I decided to. I haven’t felt like some outside force was taking over my movements or making me act like a puppet or anything.
Have you felt emotionally flat or less able to show feelings than you used to?

I don’t know… I wouldn’t say emotionally flat, exactly. I still feel things. I get upset, I get frustrated, I can feel hurt when people act like I’m making things up. So it’s not like I’m empty or nothing matters.

Maybe I don’t show it the same way all the time, but I think that’s because I’m tired of having to explain myself. Sometimes I probably look blank or quiet because I’m holding it in, or I’m trying not to start crying or get angry in front of people. But inside, no, I don’t feel like my feelings are gone.

I mean, if you mean do I laugh less or talk less sometimes, maybe, but I haven’t really thought of it as not being able to feel. It’s more like I’m worn down.
Do you believe your family is taking your money through ordinary means, or do you think they’re using something impossible, like supernatural powers or advanced technology, to do it?

No, not like supernatural powers or some machine or anything like that. I’m not saying they have special powers. I’m saying they’re doing it in normal ways, but they’re covering it up so it looks like nothing happened.

Like they keep pointing at the bank papers and saying, “See, nothing was taken,” but that doesn’t answer everything. Papers can be made to look a certain way, or money can be moved through bills and things that sound normal. That’s what I mean. The bills, the fundraiser stuff, the trip plans—those are the kinds of things they use to explain where money went, like it’s all accounted for, but I know it isn’t right.

That’s why I keep asking them and confronting them, because they act like I should just accept what they say. But I’ve known for over a year that they’re hiding my money somehow. Not magic, not technology, just people lying and using regular things to cover it up.
Before this started, did people often tell you that you were too suspicious or had trouble trusting them?

I’m not really sure how to answer that, because I don’t remember people saying it like that before. Like, not in those words. I’ve always been someone who asks questions if something doesn’t seem right, and maybe some people don’t like that, but I don’t know that they were telling me I was “too suspicious” before all this.

I mean, I didn’t just go around accusing everybody of things. I trusted people when they acted trustworthy. If somebody gave me a reason not to, then of course I’d be careful. I think that’s normal. But I can’t really think of a time before where people were always saying I had a problem trusting them.

Maybe they’d say I worry too much sometimes, or that I overthink, but that’s different. I don’t know. It’s hard to remember exactly, because when people say things now, they make it sound like I’ve always been this way, and I don’t think that’s fair.
Do you ever feel that things like TV shows, radio, or strangers’ comments are sending messages specifically to you?

No… not really like the TV or radio is talking to me or sending me secret messages. That’s not what I mean when I say something is going on.

It’s more about my family and people around me, and the money. That’s why I came in, because they keep acting like the bank papers settle everything, like if the papers don’t show it plainly then I’m supposed to just drop it. But I’ve known for over a year that they’re hiding my money somehow. They use normal things to cover it up—bills, fundraiser stuff, trip plans, things that sound reasonable when they say them out loud—so then if I question it, I look like the problem.

And it’s frustrating because everyone keeps repeating, “Look at the statements, nothing was taken,” but I’m telling them the whole point is that they’re making it look that way. I keep confronting them because nobody will just tell the truth. So no, it’s not strangers on TV sending me messages. It’s people I know covering things up and expecting me to ignore it.
Because of this situation, has your ability to work or handle your usual daily responsibilities gone down a lot?

Not really in the way you mean, I don’t think. I mean, the arguing about the money has caused a lot of stress, yes, and it takes up time because I keep having to ask questions and try to get people to explain things straight. But aside from that, I still do the things I normally have to do.

I make my own food, I keep up with my meals. I get myself to the county clinic when I’m supposed to, and I go to my assistance appointments. I keep my things in order at home the way I always have. It’s not like I’m just lying around unable to do anything or forgetting how to take care of myself.

The problem is the money situation and how everyone keeps acting like I’m supposed to ignore it. That causes arguments, yes. But my regular daily responsibilities, the basic stuff, I’m still handling that.
Has anyone else ever thought it was possible that your family was taking your money?

No, that’s the thing—everyone acts like I’m the only one who sees it. My family and even some friends keep saying, “The bank papers show nothing was taken,” like that proves everything. But I keep telling them, if they’re hiding it right, then of course the papers are going to look normal. That’s the whole point.

It’s been over a year of this. I know they’re moving it around or covering it somehow, using things that sound normal—bills, fundraisers, trip plans, little explanations here and there—so if I ask questions, they can say I’m making trouble. And then everybody looks at me like I’m the problem because I keep bringing it up.

So, no, I don’t think anyone has really stood up and said, “Yes, maybe she’s right.” They mostly just repeat what my family says or tell me to drop it. But I can’t drop it when it’s my money. I came here because nobody will tell the truth, and I have to keep confronting them until somebody finally admits what’s going on.

They might get impatient or say, “You’re not making sense,” but I think that’s more because they don’t like what I’m saying, not because I’m jumping around for no reason. I know what I mean when I’m talking. Sometimes I have to back up and explain the beginning, then the middle, because people keep interrupting or pretending they don’t understand.

So… no, I haven’t noticed my speech being hard to follow like that. People just don’t listen right.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is a Schneiderian first-rank psychotic symptom that would favor schizophrenia-spectrum psychosis over delusional disorder or paranoid personality disorder.
doctor.question: Have you felt that other people can read your thoughts?

target_item.reason: The question asks about thought broadcasting (believing others can read one's thoughts), which is not described in the provided symptom profile. The delusion profile is specifically about money being hidden or taken.

patient.answer:
Read my thoughts? No… I don’t think so. I mean, I don’t know how that would even work, exactly. Sometimes people act like they know what I’m going to say before I say it, or they jump in and assume what I mean, and that bothers me because it’s like they’ve already decided what I’m thinking. But that’s not the same as actually reading my thoughts, I guess.

I’ve had people look at me a certain way, like they think they’ve got me figured out, and I’ll be sitting there thinking, “You don’t know what’s in my head.” But I wouldn’t say I feel like they can literally hear my thoughts or anything like that. It’s more that people make assumptions and then treat those assumptions like facts. So… no, not really.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is a fixed non-bizarre persecutory delusion without broader schizophrenic symptoms, helping distinguish delusional disorder from schizophrenia-spectrum and mood disorders.
doctor.question: Aside from your family and friends hiding your money, have you believed that anyone else was trying to harm you or plot against you?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I came in because my family and friends keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken, but for over a year I’ve known they’re hiding my money and using bills, fundraisers, and trip plans to cover it up, so I have to keep confronting them until they tell the truth.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about whether there are other fixed paranoid or persecutory beliefs beyond the belief that family and friends are hiding money.

patient.answer:
I mean… yes, but it’s mostly connected to the money. It’s not like I walk around thinking every stranger is after me or something. It’s people who are involved, or who know what’s going on and won’t admit it. My family and some friends keep acting like I’m making it up because they say the bank papers don’t show anything was taken, but those papers don’t explain everything. They keep pointing to the papers like that’s supposed to end the conversation, and it doesn’t.

For over a year I’ve known they’ve been hiding my money. They cover it up with bills, and these little stories about fundraisers, and trip plans, like money is going here or there, but it never adds up right. Then when I ask questions, they act offended or say I’m being difficult. That feels like plotting to me, because if nobody did anything wrong, why keep dodging it? Why keep making it look like the money went toward normal things?

That’s why I keep confronting them. I know everyone says I should stop bringing it up, but I can’t just let people lie to my face and then tell me I’m the problem. I’m not saying someone is going to jump out and hurt me, but I do believe they’re working together to keep the truth from me until I get tired and drop it. And I’m not going to, because I need them to finally tell the truth.

doctor.intent: Differentiate a persistent delusional disorder from schizophrenia-spectrum psychosis by checking for negative symptoms, especially diminished emotional expression or motivation.
doctor.question: Have you noticed yourself becoming much less interested in things you used to care about?

target_item.reason: The question asks about loss of interest or anhedonia, which is not covered by the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I don’t know… I wouldn’t say I’ve become much less interested, exactly. I mean, some things feel harder to enjoy when there’s all this stress and people keep acting like I’m the one causing problems, but that’s different from not caring anymore.

Like, I still care about the things I cared about. I still notice them. I still want things to be normal. It’s just sometimes my mind is busy with everything else, so maybe I don’t sit and do things the same way I used to. But I don’t think I’ve lost interest in everything or anything like that.

So… no, not really. Not that I’ve noticed.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been a clear period of markedly increased goal-directed activity, which would help distinguish a delusional disorder or schizophrenia-spectrum psychosis from a manic psychosis.
doctor.question: During this past year, have there been times when you were much more active than usual, constantly taking on tasks or pursuing plans?

target_item.reason: The doctor's question is about periods of unusually increased activity or goal-directed behavior, which relates to manic or hypomanic symptoms; the provided symptom profile only covers delusions, functioning, impairment related to the delusion, and duration.

patient.answer:
Much more active than usual? I don’t think so… not in the way you’re saying, like constantly taking on tasks or making all these plans. I mean, I’ve had times where I’m busy or I’m trying to get things sorted out, but I wouldn’t say I suddenly had all this extra energy or started doing a bunch of things I normally wouldn’t do.

Sometimes if there’s something on my mind, I’ll keep going over it and I might make calls or try to organize things or write stuff down, but that feels more like I’m trying to handle what’s in front of me, not like I’m just full of energy and chasing plans. I’m not someone who’s out there starting ten projects or running around doing everything. So… no, I haven’t really noticed that.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the belief is non-bizarre and circumscribed versus part of a broader schizophrenic process by checking for passivity experiences/thought insertion, which would strongly favor schizophrenia.
doctor.question: Have you ever felt that thoughts were being put into your mind by someone or something outside you?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I came in because my family and friends keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken, but for over a year I’ve known they’re hiding my money and using bills, fundraisers, and trip plans to cover it up, so I have to keep confronting them until they tell the truth.
target_item.reason: The question asks about a possible delusional belief involving thoughts being inserted by an outside force, which falls under delusions.

patient.answer:
No… I don’t think it’s like thoughts being put in my mind. It’s not like some outside thing is placing words in my head or controlling what I think.

What I’m saying is different. I came in because my family and friends keep acting like the bank papers prove nothing happened, like that should just shut me up, but those papers don’t explain where the money really went. For over a year I’ve known they’ve been hiding it, and then they cover it with bills, fundraisers, trip plans, all these reasons that sound normal if you don’t look too closely. But I do look closely, and it doesn’t add up.

So the thoughts aren’t being put there by somebody else. I’m thinking about it because it’s happening, and because they keep denying it. That’s why I keep confronting them. I need them to stop hiding behind paperwork and excuses and just tell the truth.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the delusional belief began abruptly or has been longstanding, to distinguish acute/transient psychosis from persistent delusional disorder or schizophrenia-spectrum illness.
doctor.question: Did this belief that your family was hiding your money come on suddenly?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This has been going on since my income dropped, about a year and two months ago.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about when and how the belief began, which relates most directly to the duration/onset of the delusional belief.

patient.answer:
Not suddenly, no. It wasn’t like one day I woke up and thought that out of nowhere. It’s been going on since my income dropped… about a year and two months ago, something like that.

That’s when things started not making sense to me. I kept noticing the money situation wasn’t lining up, and the more time went on, the more it felt like people were explaining it away instead of actually answering me. So it built up from there. It’s been over a year now, not some sudden thing.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are Schneiderian/passivity phenomena, especially experiences of being controlled, to distinguish schizophrenia-spectrum psychosis from a persistent delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Have you felt that someone or something was controlling your actions or movements?

target_item.reason: The question asks about feeling that an outside force controls actions or movements, but the provided symptom profile only covers fixed delusional beliefs about family hiding money and related functioning/duration, not experiences of external control of movements.

patient.answer:
No… I don’t think so. I mean, nobody is moving my arms or making me walk somewhere or anything like that. I’m in control of what I do.

Sometimes people pressure you, you know, or they keep saying things until you feel pushed to respond, but that’s not the same as controlling my body. If I make a call or go somewhere or say something, that’s me doing it because I decided to. I haven’t felt like some outside force was taking over my movements or making me act like a puppet or anything.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are any prominent negative symptoms, which would help distinguish schizophrenia from delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Have you felt emotionally flat or less able to show feelings than you used to?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about emotional flatness or reduced emotional expression, which is not covered by the listed symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I don’t know… I wouldn’t say emotionally flat, exactly. I still feel things. I get upset, I get frustrated, I can feel hurt when people act like I’m making things up. So it’s not like I’m empty or nothing matters.

Maybe I don’t show it the same way all the time, but I think that’s because I’m tired of having to explain myself. Sometimes I probably look blank or quiet because I’m holding it in, or I’m trying not to start crying or get angry in front of people. But inside, no, I don’t feel like my feelings are gone.

I mean, if you mean do I laugh less or talk less sometimes, maybe, but I haven’t really thought of it as not being able to feel. It’s more like I’m worn down.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the delusional belief is culturally implausible/bizarre, which best distinguishes delusional disorder from schizophrenia-spectrum psychoses given the chronic isolated persecutory theme and absence of hallucinations, thought insertion, control, disorganization, mania, or major depression.
doctor.question: Do you believe your family is taking your money through ordinary means, or do you think they’re using something impossible, like supernatural powers or advanced technology, to do it?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I came in because my family and friends keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken, but for over a year I’ve known they’re hiding my money and using bills, fundraisers, and trip plans to cover it up, so I have to keep confronting them until they tell the truth.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about the nature of the fixed belief that the family is taking money, specifically whether it is based on ordinary means or impossible/supernatural means, so it directly concerns the delusion.

patient.answer:
No, not like supernatural powers or some machine or anything like that. I’m not saying they have special powers. I’m saying they’re doing it in normal ways, but they’re covering it up so it looks like nothing happened.

Like they keep pointing at the bank papers and saying, “See, nothing was taken,” but that doesn’t answer everything. Papers can be made to look a certain way, or money can be moved through bills and things that sound normal. That’s what I mean. The bills, the fundraiser stuff, the trip plans—those are the kinds of things they use to explain where money went, like it’s all accounted for, but I know it isn’t right.

That’s why I keep asking them and confronting them, because they act like I should just accept what they say. But I’ve known for over a year that they’re hiding my money somehow. Not magic, not technology, just people lying and using regular things to cover it up.

inference.note: Ruled out mood-congruent psychotic mood disorders as primary candidates: repeated denial of sustained elevated/irritable manic syndrome and lack of clear major depressive episode with psychotic features. Persistent, non-bizarre persecutory delusion >1 year without hallucinations, thought insertion/broadcasting/control, disorganization, or negative symptoms strengthens F22; F20.0 and F23.3 remain less likely differentials, and F60.0 remains a trait differential.

doctor.intent: Distinguish a persistent delusional disorder from paranoid personality disorder by determining whether this fixed suspicious belief is a change from the patient’s longstanding baseline or part of a lifelong pervasive pattern.
doctor.question: Before this started, did people often tell you that you were too suspicious or had trouble trusting them?

target_item.reason: The question is about whether there was a longstanding pattern of suspiciousness or distrust before the delusion began, and the provided symptom profiles only describe the current delusion, duration, and functioning after it started.

patient.answer:
I’m not really sure how to answer that, because I don’t remember people saying it like that before. Like, not in those words. I’ve always been someone who asks questions if something doesn’t seem right, and maybe some people don’t like that, but I don’t know that they were telling me I was “too suspicious” before all this.

I mean, I didn’t just go around accusing everybody of things. I trusted people when they acted trustworthy. If somebody gave me a reason not to, then of course I’d be careful. I think that’s normal. But I can’t really think of a time before where people were always saying I had a problem trusting them.

Maybe they’d say I worry too much sometimes, or that I overthink, but that’s different. I don’t know. It’s hard to remember exactly, because when people say things now, they make it sound like I’ve always been this way, and I don’t think that’s fair.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the fixed persecutory belief is accompanied by a broader pattern of ideas of reference, which would help distinguish delusional disorder from paranoid schizophrenia and paranoid personality disorder.
doctor.question: Do you ever feel that things like TV shows, radio, or strangers’ comments are sending messages specifically to you?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I came in because my family and friends keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken, but for over a year I’ve known they’re hiding my money and using bills, fundraisers, and trip plans to cover it up, so I have to keep confronting them until they tell the truth.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about possible delusional beliefs, specifically whether ordinary events or media feel like they contain special messages directed at me.

patient.answer:
No… not really like the TV or radio is talking to me or sending me secret messages. That’s not what I mean when I say something is going on.

It’s more about my family and people around me, and the money. That’s why I came in, because they keep acting like the bank papers settle everything, like if the papers don’t show it plainly then I’m supposed to just drop it. But I’ve known for over a year that they’re hiding my money somehow. They use normal things to cover it up—bills, fundraiser stuff, trip plans, things that sound reasonable when they say them out loud—so then if I question it, I look like the problem.

And it’s frustrating because everyone keeps repeating, “Look at the statements, nothing was taken,” but I’m telling them the whole point is that they’re making it look that way. I keep confronting them because nobody will just tell the truth. So no, it’s not strangers on TV sending me messages. It’s people I know covering things up and expecting me to ignore it.

inference.note: Sustained >1 year non-bizarre persecutory/theft delusion without hallucinations, thought insertion/broadcasting/control, disorganization, negative symptoms, mood episodes, or bizarre content makes F22 most likely. Duration rules against F23.3, so it is removed. F20.0 remains less likely due to lack of other schizophrenic symptoms. F60.0 remains a differential but is less favored because suspiciousness appears not longstanding premorbidly.

doctor.intent: Determine whether this fixed persecutory belief is causing a marked decline in everyday functioning, which best separates delusional disorder from schizophrenia.
doctor.question: Because of this situation, has your ability to work or handle your usual daily responsibilities gone down a lot?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: Other than the arguments about the money, I still handle my own meals, get to the county clinic and assistance appointments, and keep my things in order the same way I always have.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether daily responsibilities or work functioning have markedly declined because of the situation, which directly matches this profile item about functioning not being markedly impaired apart from the delusion’s impact.

patient.answer:
Not really in the way you mean, I don’t think. I mean, the arguing about the money has caused a lot of stress, yes, and it takes up time because I keep having to ask questions and try to get people to explain things straight. But aside from that, I still do the things I normally have to do.

I make my own food, I keep up with my meals. I get myself to the county clinic when I’m supposed to, and I go to my assistance appointments. I keep my things in order at home the way I always have. It’s not like I’m just lying around unable to do anything or forgetting how to take care of myself.

The problem is the money situation and how everyone keeps acting like I’m supposed to ignore it. That causes arguments, yes. But my regular daily responsibilities, the basic stuff, I’m still handling that.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the suspicious belief is non-bizarre/plausible and circumscribed, which best distinguishes delusional disorder from schizophrenia-spectrum psychosis and paranoid personality disorder.
doctor.question: Has anyone else ever thought it was possible that your family was taking your money?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I came in because my family and friends keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken, but for over a year I’ve known they’re hiding my money and using bills, fundraisers, and trip plans to cover it up, so I have to keep confronting them until they tell the truth.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about whether the belief that family is taking money is shared or supported by others, which directly relates to the delusional belief about money being hidden or stolen despite others saying the evidence does not support it.

patient.answer:
No, that’s the thing—everyone acts like I’m the only one who sees it. My family and even some friends keep saying, “The bank papers show nothing was taken,” like that proves everything. But I keep telling them, if they’re hiding it right, then of course the papers are going to look normal. That’s the whole point.

It’s been over a year of this. I know they’re moving it around or covering it somehow, using things that sound normal—bills, fundraisers, trip plans, little explanations here and there—so if I ask questions, they can say I’m making trouble. And then everybody looks at me like I’m the problem because I keep bringing it up.

So, no, I don’t think anyone has really stood up and said, “Yes, maybe she’s right.” They mostly just repeat what my family says or tell me to drop it. But I can’t drop it when it’s my money. I came here because nobody will tell the truth, and I have to keep confronting them until somebody finally admits what’s going on.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a persistent, non-bizarre persecutory delusion focused on family/friends hiding or stealing money for over one year, with strong conviction despite contrary evidence. There are no hallucinations, thought insertion, thought broadcasting, passivity experiences, disorganized speech, prominent negative symptoms, manic syndrome, or clear major depressive episode. Functioning is largely preserved outside the delusional conflict, supporting delusional disorder rather than schizophrenia or paranoid personality disorder.
